method: The owner's section-17 fields were extracted on 2026-10-27 only from the verbatim excerpts already in research_evidence.json (no new sources were read). Three extractors each took a third of the spots (extractor A: anchor-point to lakey-peak, B: lobitos to salsa-brava, C: shipstern-bluff to waimea-bay). Every value cites the claims it rests on (source key, claim index, the claim's excerpt copied exactly); a field with no supporting excerpt is not_documented with a null value, and a field whose excerpts state different values (for directions, best directions 45 deg or more apart; overlapping ranges agree) is conflicting, with one entry per stated value and the sources stating it. Directions are degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale the source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or body-relative) and are converted only where the source states the conversion or by stated arithmetic (1 m = 3.28 ft, noted). tide.local_tide_data is app data from data/tide_stations.json (docs/tides.md), not research evidence, and has no citations. scripts/generate_spot_research_docs.py checks every citation against the evidence file mechanically. A judgement check re-read every field of 15 spots (five per extractor: units, face versus swell height, FROM directions, whether the excerpt states the value) and a targeted re-read covered fields whose note said the value was not a stated preference; the changes are recorded per spot under judgement_check.

bathymetry.value: a rocky headland about 100 m long, often partly sand-covered, with a groyne; the beach bar (steeper than the rock) and an inner sand bank shape the barrel; sand bypassing from the Tweed River has filled it in

citations.excerpt: Kirra Point is a natural rocky headland that extends about 100 m into the sea. A sand layer often covers part of the rocky reef substrate.
Kirra owes much of its excellent surf quality to waves breaking over the beach bar.
the angle of the groyne and inner sand bank consistently tubes across Kirra Point
TypePoint-break...BottomSandy with rock
In May 1972, the Government of Queensland built a groyne, now called "big groyne", extending Kirra Point, to trap sand on Coolangatta beach to the south.
In 1974, a beach fill project was undertaken and a groyne was extended 400 rn at the head of Kirra Point.
In 1995 30 metres was taken off Big Groyne to help fight erosion at Greenmount Beach. Both groynes have been almost completely covered by sand from the sand pumping.
In June 1996, a length of about 30 m of the seaward end of the groyne was removed.
Today sand pumping across the Tweed River mouth has filled it in and changed its character.
The stretch of sand in front of Kirra is rock hard, however, and in the last run of solid swell offered the finest jewels along the entire Superbank.
However, the quality of the last section, Kirra, which has long been regarded as one of the world's best waves prior to the formation of the Superbank, has suffered.
Kirra is currently producing a fun longboard-style wave.

bathymetry.note: The 1997 assessment describes a natural rocky headland about 100 m long often covered by sand and says the quality comes from waves breaking over the beach bar, National Surfing Reserves credits the groyne angle and inner sand bank, and WannaSurf gives sand with rock; Wikipedia says Tweed River sand pumping has filled it in and changed its character, WSL that the sand was rock hard in the last solid swell, and the 2024 committee notes a fun longboard-style wave; the groyne history dates differ (Wikipedia: built May 1972, 30 m removed 1995; the 1997 assessment: extended 400 m in 1974, 30 m removed June 1996).
